DESCRIPTION. Technical field of the invention The present invention relates to a compound of formula I, t: wherein R is selected from the group consisting of -H, -F, -Cl, -Br, -I, -N0 2 , - CH 3 , and -C 2 H 5 ; X is selected from the group consisting of -F, -Cl, -Br, and -I; and pharmaceutically acceptable salts thereof. The present invention also relates to processes for the preparation of the compound of formula I. Prior Art Pyridazine derivatives, including pyridazinones, have an important place in medicinal chemistry research because of their pharmaceutical interest. A lot of attention has been paid on pyridazine derivatives as a potential target for the development of new drugs for the treatment of various diseases. Many reviews have been published that dictate the therapeutic potential of pyridazine derivatives, for example, Asif et ah, Medicinal Chemistry Research , 2012, 21, p. 3336-3346; Imran &Abida, Tropical Journal of Pharmaceutical Research, 2016, 15(7), p. 1579-1590; Dubey &Bhosle, Medicinal Chemistry Research, 2015, 24, p. 3579-3599; and Akhtar et al, European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry, 2016, 123, p. 256-281. These reviews mention that pyridazine derivatives possess wide variety of biological activities, for example, antiinflammatory activity, analgesic activity, antioxidant activity, anticancer activity, antiviral activity, antimicrobial activity, cardiovascular activity, antitubercular activity, antiobesity activity, antidiabetic activity, neuroprotective activity, antihypertensive activity, antifungal activity, antibacterial activity, antidepressant activity, and anticonvulsant activity. These reviews also highlight the names and structures of many pyridazine derivatives that are under clinical use for the treatment of different diseases. U.S. Patent No. 4,404,203 provides substituted 6-phenyl-3(2H)-pyridazinones as cardioactive agents. It also provides the preparation of key intermediates, for example, 6-phenyl-4,5-dihydropyridazin-3(2H)-one and 6-phenylpyridazin- 3(2H)-one for the preparation of substituted 6-phenyl-3(2H)-pyridazinones. Imran and Khan, Medicinal Chemistry Research , 2017, 26, p. 1481 provide some coumarin derivatives of pharmaceutical interest. OBJECT The primary object of the present invention is to providenovel pyridazinone derivatives and process for their preparation which may be useful as potential drug candidates for the treatment of various diseases, for example, bacterial infection, fungal infection, oxidative stress, cancer, hypertension, inflammation, pain, diabetes, and convulsion. STATEMENT The present inventors have identified and prepared novel pyridazinone derivatives of formula I of pharmaceutical interest. These compounds may be useful as potential drug candidates for the treatment of various diseases, for example, bacterial infection, fungal infection, oxidative stress, cancer, hypertension, inflammation, pain, diabetes, and convulsion. These compounds may also serve as lead compounds to develop new drugs. The present invention also relates to processes for the preparation of the compound of formula I. The dotted line in the structure of the compound of formula I indicates that the ring structure may contain a double bond. As used herein, " pharmaceutically acceptable salts " refer to derivatives of the compound of formula I, wherein the parent compound is modified by making acid or base salts thereof. Examples of pharmaceutically acceptable salts include hydrochloride salt, sulphate salt, phosphate salt, nitrate salt, acetate salt, tartarate salt, citrate salt, sodium salt, and potassium salt. EXAMPLES Example 1: Preparation of 4-oxo-4-phenylbutanoic acid To a solution of succinic anhydride (0.1 moles) in benzene (50 mL), anhydrous aluminium chloride (0.125 moles) was added in small portions with stirring over a period of 2 hours. The reaction mixture was refluxed for 2 hours. After completion of the reaction, the excess of benzene was removed by steam distillation. The reaction mixture was dissolved in sodium hydroxide solution, filtered, and hydrochloric acid was added to it. The solid mass obtained was filtered, washed with cold water, dried and recrystallized from methanol to obtain the title compound having a melting point of 1 l3°C to 1 l6°C. Similarly, different 4-oxo-4-(substitutedphenyl)butanoic acid can also be prepared from different substituted benzene. The different 4-oxo-4- (substitutedphenyl)butanoic acid can easily be converted to 6- (substitutedphenyl)-4,5-dihydropyridazin-3(2H)-one and 6- (substitutedphenyl)pyridazine-3(2H)-one by following the methods provided in the prior art. Example 2: Preparation of 2-(2-oxo-2-(2-oxo-2H-chromen-3-yl)ethyl)-6- phenyl-4,5-dihydropyridazin-3(2H)-one 6-Phenyl-4,5-dihydropyridazin-3(2H)-one (0.1 mole) and 3-(2-bromoacetyl)-2H- chromen-2-one (0.1 mole) were refluxed for about 18 hours in acetone in the presence of potassium carbonate. The contents were reduced to half of its volume and poured on ice cold water. The precipitate was filtered, washed with water and then recrystallized from ethanol. Yield: 55% M.P.: l60°C-l62°C Example 3: Preparation of 2-(2-oxo-2-(2-oxo-2H-chromen-3-yl)ethyl)-6- phenylpyridazin-3(2H)-one To an acetic acid solution of 2-(2-oxo-2-(2-oxo-2H-chromen-3-yl)ethyl)-6- phenyl-4,5-dihydropyridazin-3(2H)-one (0.1 mole), another acetic solution of bromine (0.15 moles) was added with stirring for about thirty minutes. The precipitate was filtered, washed with water and then recrystallized from acetic acid. Yield: 70% M.P.: 20l°C-203°C Additional advantages and modification will readily occur to those skilled in the art.
